run: plan item 4.3: the modulation engines' polarisation on synthetic known answers (a planted [1 0 1] mode in a monoclinic cell, one seed and a 60-seed sweep; the existing planted modes), both fixtures and the dev cases; arms A and A+ on the dev set before (d9cb984) and after (the code of 9a72a6f, recorded under protocol 2026-10-19.12), 2026-10-19
evidence: Plan item 4.3 (docs/AGENT_PLAN.md, phase 4; section D: 'analyze_modulations gives the wavevector, not the displacement direction of the mode. A+ takes it from the most prolate site's PC1'). The modulation engines returned each ordered point's q, ratio, percentile and sigma but not the direction its atoms move, so arm A+ took a modulation claim's direction from the PC1 of the element's most prolate site (PC1/PC2 >= 1.3), a rule of its own the app does not have, and a model had no number to quote by reference. The polarisation as built is the leading eigenvector of the real part of the element's cross-spectral tensor at q, (1/m) sum_s Re[U_s(q) U_s(q)^H] / (n_s tr C_s), whose trace is the power: the mode's mean-square displacement tensor (the imaginary part is antisymmetric, an elliptical mode's circulation, and carries no axis); share = lambda_1 / tr. Known answers: both sites of an element displaced 0.1 A along the direct-lattice [1 0 1] of a monoclinic cell (beta = 105 deg; [1 0 1] is 14 deg from the Cartesian (1, 0, 1)) at q = (1/2, 0, 0), in antiphase, over 0.06 A of noise in 128 cells: the polarisation lies within 5 deg of the planted direction and its share above 0.95, in both engines (the fixture's case: 0.9975, -0.0229, 1 as [u v w], share 0.9993); over 60 seeds the mean squared angle is within 25 % of twice the square of the sampling error sigma / (delta sqrt(m n)) = 0.0375 rad per component, none beyond 10 deg, every share above 0.95. The planted modes the engine already had read along their axes: the doubled Nb along z (share 0.997), the long-wave repro's order along z and its long wave along y, the general-q order along z under a long wave along y. dev-zone-boundary: the Ti order at (0, 0, 1/2) is 5.5 deg from its planted [0 0 1] (one site over 512 cells: 1.5 deg of sampling error per component, so a 3.6-sigma draw; the PC1 A+ read before is an estimator of the same noise and scored 6.0 deg), share 1 (one site at a zone-boundary point: a rank-1 tensor); the decoy Sr long wave is 4.7 deg from its own axis. Arms A and A+ on dev before and after: every arm A and D record identical, every score identical; two A+ records move. dev-zone-boundary__A+: the Ti claim's direction [-0.03 0.1 1] -> [-0.05 0.09 1] (5.96 -> 5.88 deg as scored, within the 15 deg tolerance) and its analyze_modulations reading gains the polarisation. dev-weak-order-a__A+: the Nb claim had no direction (no prolate Nb site: the order is far below the thermal width) and now has [0.17 0.06 1] (10 deg from the planted axis; the truth names q only, so the score is unchanged) and its reading gains the polarisation. The test set was not run. What the model sees changes in analyze_modulations' result only (the polarisation rows and their note appear only with an ordered point; the Demo has none). Approved by the manager on the user's delegation, 2026-10-19.
proposed_fix: Both engines (rmc_toolkits/modulations.py mode_polarisation and element_spectrum; workers/modulations.js modePolarisation, elementSpectrum and tensorAt, pcaKde.js's Jacobi eigensolver) give every zone-boundary point and strongest mode a polarisation {direction: a Cartesian unit vector; uvw: the same as a direct-lattice [u v w] = M^-T d, largest component 1, the form of list_sites' pc1_uvw; share: lambda_1 / tr}, both in the sense that makes the closest crystal axis acute (crystalOrientationRows' rule, ties within AXIS_TIE_RTOL = 1e-9 to the first axis), null without power. The golden (modulations_fixture.json) pins every polarisation; its generator refuses a polarisation whose two largest eigenvalues lie within 1e-6 of the trace or whose sense is decided near the tie tolerance, and gains the monoclinic case. analyze_modulations shows each ordered point's polarisation (a polarisation row: q, uvw to two decimals, share, nearest_low_index within LOW_INDEX_CONE_DEG = 15 deg) and says it in the point's check ('polarised along [0 0 1] (5.5 deg off; 100 % of the power at q)'); the dataShape declares the row; the tool gets its own result budget (MODULATION_RESULT_BUDGET = 4000: three elements with an ordered point run to 2,889 characters with the checks on dev-zone-boundary, ~110 within the default 3000). Arm A+ reads a modulation claim's direction from the engine's polarisation at the q that decided the order (two decimals, as its other direction claims) and records each ordered point's polarisation in its reading. facts.modulation is unchanged. Commits 70d2829 (engines), 6da2b15 (tool), 9a72a6f (arm A+). Approved by the manager on the user's delegation, 2026-10-19.
